validated_reference_adapter.comparison_method: The Ezekiel adapter is byte-identical to the validated Jeremiah adapter after the complete expected deterministic replacement set: T547 to T548; Jeremiah/jeremiah/Jer/JER/jer to Ezekiel/ezekiel/Ezek/EZEK/ezek; 1364 and 1,364 to 1273 and 1,273; Jer.1.1 to Ezek.1.1; and Jer.52.34 to Ezek.48.35.

summary: The T548 Ezekiel materializer is a faithful book-specific adapter of the validated Jeremiah implementation. Every audited task, path, book code, verse inventory, schema, identifier, sidecar partition, postcheck command, and finalizer binding is internally consistent. No stale Jeremiah literal, stale Jeremiah verse constant, malformed Ezekiel name, or unexpected code delta remains.

evidence.observation: The module identifies Ezekiel, T548, candidate-only scope, and the non-authorizing boundary.
The repository root, M7 model root, Ezekiel review directory, Ezekiel chunk file, adjudicated route, and canonical WEB witness path resolve to the intended scoped locations.
Generated artifact references and write targets consistently name book_strategy/Ezek.md, reviews/Ezek, book_chunks/Ezek, and receipts/Ezek_completion_v2.json.
A read-only exact book-prefix scan found 1,273 Ezekiel witness rows, beginning Ezek.1.1 and ending Ezek.48.35.
The adapter filters exactly Ezek.*, requires 1,273 rows, and fail-closes on endpoints other than Ezek.1.1 and Ezek.48.35.
Span parsing is book-locked to Ezekiel and the assembled route must exactly reproduce the ordered 1,273-verse inventory.
The three decision-local route roles are exactly hebrew_textual_oracle_form, literary_prophetic_cycle, and canonical_retrieval_premortem, with stable ID codes.
Each route unit must carry exactly one review for each role, an allowed verdict, bespoke support and counterevidence, and structurally valid challenges.
The route must identify Ezek, be frozen, provide a non-empty count-consistent unit list, and satisfy disposition, hold, and primary-support invariants.
Decision, challenge, appeal, primary, peer, boss, and postcluster IDs consistently use M7_sol-Ezek, EZEK-V2, or ezek-v2 namespaces.
Decision relation, appeal, sidecar replacement, and role-artifact rows consistently carry Ezekiel-specific schemas, book codes, and note or dissent IDs.
The packet records WEB plus OSHB/UXLC locators without claiming independent WLC witnesses and fail-closes on invented local LXX, DSS, rabbinic, or Second-Temple sources.

checks.subject: sidecar payload generation and book partition filtering

evidence.observation: All and only the three required sidecars are emitted, every replacement row is book-scoped to Ezek, and the payload explicitly requests replacement of existing Ezekiel rows.
Finalizer sidecar digests filter strictly on row.book == Ezek and use the same canonicalized row encoding as the generic receipt and completion-bundle contracts.
The generic atomic installer accepts the emitted reviews/Ezek/sidecar_rows_v2.json payload, replaces only the requested book partition, and fail-closes on mismatched book or non-authorizing flags.

checks.subject: materialization closure is deliberately invalid before sidecar install and checker review

evidence.observation: The first pass hash-binds local artifacts but explicitly records pending checker/sidecar failure and invalidates the completion receipt; it does not falsely declare completion.

The adapter invokes exact coverage, the official whole-Bible chunk-map validator, review/sidecar parity, literary quality with required artifacts, and corrective-depth validation, all bound to Ezek and M7_sol.
The command set matches the generic receipt writer's five required gates; the receipt writer adds require-final-artifacts when it reruns review coverage after the final postcheck exists.

checks.subject: finalizer hash, identity, verdict, and receipt bindings

evidence.observation: Finalization accepts only a verdict stored in reviews/Ezek, binds the current chunk, packet, relation, and Ezekiel sidecar-partition hashes, enforces the correct pass/pass_with_holds status and a distinct role-separated checker, and rejects unresolved findings.

The final postcheck records every required current hash and decision ID, preserves the same-model limitation, then invokes the generic receipt writer last with --book Ezek and fail-closes if it refuses.
The adapter's final postcheck and receipt fields align with the generic completion bundle's book, hash, checker, decision-inventory, verdict, and completion-state closure checks.
Case-insensitive exact scans found zero occurrences of Jer, Jeremiah, jer, JER, 1364, 1,364, 52.34, T547, or ezekemiah. Expected Ezekiel/T548/1,273 constants are present.
A read-only Python compile check completed successfully without importing or executing the materializer.

runtime_preconditions.condition: reviews/Ezek/adjudicated_route_draft_v2.json must exist, identify book Ezek, be frozen, and satisfy the adapter's exact role and 1,273-verse coverage contract before the materialization pass is run.
runtime_preconditions.reason: The route did not yet exist at audit time, so this audit validates adapter correctness rather than claiming a successful materialization run.

runtime_preconditions.condition: After materialization, install reviews/Ezek/sidecar_rows_v2.json through checks/install_book_sidecar_rows_v2.py --book Ezek before finalization.
runtime_preconditions.reason: The materializer intentionally does not mutate shared sidecars.

runtime_preconditions.condition: A fresh role-separated checker verdict in reviews/Ezek must bind the current chunks, packets, relations, and Ezekiel sidecar partitions before --finalize may write the final postcheck and invoke the receipt writer.
runtime_preconditions.reason: Static adapter correctness is not a completion receipt and is not cross-model convergence.
